title: How FlexLine Workout Relief Is Figured from the Fee
content:
**Rule — FlexLine Personal Lines of Credit.** The way the workout relief is figured follows the late fees booked on the line in the last 12 months and the amount past due: when two or more late fees were booked in the last 12 months, the relief is the fee less 5.00 USD, which the borrower keeps paying, never below 0.00; when exactly one late fee was booked in the last 12 months and the amount past due is below the fee, the relief is the amount past due; otherwise the relief is the whole fee.

*The fee* is the late fee the relief is booked against. *The late fees counted* are the late-fee entries on the line dated after the same day of the month 12 months before the relief date. *The amount past due* is the one on Larkspur's record of the line on the relief date.

## Decision table

| Late fees booked in the last 12 months | Amount past due against the fee | Relief as figured |
|---|---|---|
| two or more | any | the fee less 5.00, never below 0.00 |
| exactly one | below the fee | the amount past due |
| exactly one | equal to the fee or more | the whole fee |
| none | any | the whole fee |

## Hypothetical cases

- Two late fees in the window, fee 18.50: relief figured at 13.50.
- Two late fees in the window, fee 4.00: 4.00 less 5.00 is below 0.00, so 0.00.
- One late fee in the window, fee 25.00, amount past due 16.30: 16.30.
- One late fee in the window, fee 25.00, amount past due 140.00: 25.00.
